stories.headline: Cyclone: Andhra fishermen asked not to venture into sea
stories.title: Cyclone: Andhra fishermen asked not to venture into sea
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Amaravati: With the deep depression hovering over parts of the Bay of Bengal, the APSDMA on Monday asked Andhra Pradesh fishermen not to venture into the sea.
Andhra Pradesh State Disaster Management Authority (APSDMA) managing director Prakhar Jain said that squally winds are expected to strike the coastal regions of the state, accompanied by heavy rains.
He also advised farmers and people to take precautions.

The deep depression hovering over parts of the Bay of Bengal is likely to intensify into a cyclonic storm by Monday evening, a severe cyclonic storm by November 17 and further into a very severe cyclonic storm near Andhra Pradesh coast around November 19, compelling the southern state to brace for its third cyclone within three weeks.

The deep depression over Southeast and adjoining Southwest Bay of Bengal moved north to northwestwards with a speed of eight km per hour in the past six hours and lay centred over the same region at 5:30 am today, an official release from the Meteorological Department said.
The southern state was battered by two cyclones in quick succession recently -- Arnab and Murasu -- flattening lakhs of acres of crops and causing a loss estimated at nearly Rs 7,000 crore.

stories.headline: Cyclone Akvan to cross Andhra coast between Nellore and Tuni by November 20 noon, says IMD
stories.title: Cyclone Akvan to cross Andhra coast between Nellore and Tuni by November 20 noon, says IMD
stories.summary: Andhra fishermen still awaiting compensation for Cyclone Arnab’s losses are told to stay ashore till November 20 ahead of Akvan
reasons: source: event has 2 copies, primary source counted once
corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Cyclone Akvan, expected to form over the Bay of Bengal on Monday evening, is very likely to cross the Andhra Pradesh and Yanam coasts between Nellore and Tuni by noon on November 20 as a very severe cyclonic storm, the India Meteorological Department (IMD) said in its forecast on Monday (November 16, 2026).
Winds at landfall may reach 120-130 kmph, gusting to 145 kmph.
That leaves about 500 km of coast in play, that is, nearly half of Andhra Pradesh’s 1,053-km shoreline.
Machilipatnam sits roughly in the middle.
Weather experts are monitoring the system as it may change its course again.
Initial forecasts had indicated that the system may move towards north coastal Andhra Pradesh.
The latest IMD bulletin places its landfall in central and south coastal Andhra Pradesh.
Previously, very severe cyclonic storm Arnab made landfall near Narsapur, part of central Andhra Pradesh, and severe cyclonic storm Murasu near Ongole in south coastal Andhra Pradesh.
Krishna district, of which Machilipatnam is a part, has seen devastating cyclones in the past, including the infamous 1977 Diviseema cyclone.
However, the district was spared much of the damage during Arnab and Murasu.
Meanwhile, the depression over the southeast Bay of Bengal concentrated into a deep depression over the southeast and southwest Bay of Bengal in the early hours of Monday (November 16, 2026).

The system moved north-northwestwards at 6 kmph during the past six hours, and at 8.30 a.m., it lay centred about 630 km east-northeast of Trincomalee in Sri Lanka, 690 km west of Sri Vijaya Puram in the Andaman and Nicobar Islands, 700 km east-southeast of Chennai in Tamil Nadu, 800 km south-southeast of Visakhapatnam in Andhra Pradesh and 910 km south of Gopalpur in Odisha.

stories.headline: Cyclone threat clouds Jagaddhatri Puja celebrations in Bengal
stories.title: Cyclone threat clouds Jagaddhatri Puja celebrations in Bengal
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: With a deep depression over the Bay of Bengal likely to intensify into a cyclone, the India Meteorological Department (IMD) on Sunday warned of rain and thunderstorms across South Bengal from Wednesday, raising the possibility of weather disruptions during Jagaddhatri Puja celebrations.
IMD said a low-pressure area over the south-east Bay of Bengal became a deep depression Monday, November 16, moving north-westwards.
At midnight, it lay 680 km from Andaman and Nicobar’s Sri Vijaya Puram, 720 km from Chennai in Tamil Nadu, 820 km from Andhra Pradesh’s Visakhapatnam, and 940 km from Odisha’s Gopalpur.

“It is very likely to move north-northwestwards, intensify further into a Cyclonic Storm over the central parts of the south and adjoining west-central Bay of Bengal on November 16 and into a Severe Cyclonic Storm over the west-central Bay of Bengal on November 17, 2026.
Thereafter, it is likely to intensify further and move northwestwards towards the Andhra Pradesh coast during the subsequent two days,” it said.
Under the influence of this system, the Regional Meteorological Centre (RMC) in Kolkata warned of rain in South Bengal from Wednesday, November 18.

It issued a yellow alert for all South Bengal districts from Thursday till the early hours of Sunday for thunderstorms, lightning, and gusty winds of 30-40 kmph at a couple of locations, coinciding with Jagaddhatri Puja in West Bengal.
This year, the main puja rituals will be performed on Wednesday, and the idols will be taken out in processions and immersed on Dashami, Thursday.

A few places in districts along the Bay of Bengal coast, South 24 Parganas, East and West Midnapore, and Jhargram are also expected to receive heavy rainfall of 7-11 cm, along with gusty winds of 40-50 kmph, on Thursday and Friday.
Light rain and thundershowers are likely in isolated pockets in South Bengal districts of Kolkata, Howrah, North and South 24 Parganas, and East and West Midnapore on Wednesday.
Dry weather will prevail over Hooghly, Jhargram, Purulia, Bankura, East and West Bardhaman, Murshidabad, and Nadia.
From Thursday onwards, all the South Bengal districts are set to experience light to moderate rain and thundershowers till Sunday.

stories.headline: India News Live Updates, 16 November 2026 | Cyclone threat: Odisha orders evacuation, Andhra bars fishermen from sea
stories.title: India News Live Updates, 16 November 2026 | Cyclone threat: Odisha orders evacuation, Andhra bars fishermen from sea
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: The Odisha government on Monday ordered the evacuation of vulnerable areas in its southern districts as a deep depression over the Bay of Bengal is expected to intensify into a very severe cyclonic storm near the Andhra Pradesh coast around November 19.
Ganjam administration has identified landslide-prone and low-lying areas for evacuation.
Odisha has faced two cyclones, Arnab and Murasu, in three weeks, with Arnab claiming 11 lives and leaving six people missing.

The India Meteorological Department (IMD) said the system, currently over the southeast and adjoining southwest Bay of Bengal, could intensify into a cyclonic storm by Monday evening, a severe cyclonic storm by November 17 and a very severe cyclonic storm by November 19.
Heavy to very heavy rainfall is forecast in parts of Odisha from November 19 to 21, with winds reaching 70 kmph.
The Andhra Pradesh State Disaster Management Authority has warned of heavy rain and squally winds along the coast and advised fishermen not to venture into the sea.
A similar advisory is in place for Odisha from November 18 until the morning of November 20, when sea conditions are expected to remain rough to very rough.

Tamil Nadu’s Chennai, Tiruvallur and Chengalpattu are likely to receive heavy rain, thunderstorms, lightning and 40-50 kmph winds from November 17, with Kanchipuram, Ranipet, Tiruvannamalai, Villupuram, Cuddalore, Mayiladuthurai and Puducherry expected to receive heavy rain from November 18.
The storm, named Akvan, is forecast to intensify into a severe cyclonic storm on Monday evening.
Tamil Nadu fishermen have also been advised to stay ashore from November 16 to 21.

stories.headline: Andhra landfall or Tamil Nadu strike? Conflicting forecasts cloud Cyclone Akvan's path
stories.title: Andhra landfall or Tamil Nadu strike? Conflicting forecasts cloud Cyclone Akvan's path
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: IMD expects Cyclone Akvan to make landfall along the Andhra Pradesh coast, while private weather forecasters point to a possible Tamil Nadu strike between Chennai and Cuddalore.
Will Cyclone Akvan strike Tamil Nadu or move towards Andhra Pradesh?
With the storm's projected trajectory subject to conflicting forecasts, residents along the eastern coast are grappling with uncertainty about where it could eventually make landfall.

While the India Meteorological Department (IMD) has maintained that the system is likely to cross the Andhra Pradesh coast, private weather forecasters suggest the cyclone could instead make landfall somewhere between Chennai and Cuddalore.

The conflicting assessments have triggered confusion, particularly among residents in coastal Tamil Nadu, who are trying to understand the potential threat and whether they need to prepare for the cyclone's impact.
According to the IMD's assessment on Sunday, a depression over the southeast and adjoining southwest Bay of Bengal is likely to intensify into a severe cyclonic storm by Tuesday.
The system is expected to move towards the Andhra Pradesh coast around Thursday.
The weather department also released a projected trajectory indicating that the cyclone would travel along the Tamil Nadu coast before making landfall in Andhra Pradesh.
However, private weather enthusiasts have offered a different assessment, suggesting a possible southward shift in the system's path that could bring it towards the Tamil Nadu coastline.
Dr VR Durai of the Regional Meteorological Centre (RMC), Chennai, told DT Next that IMD scientists rely on multiple weather prediction models to assess a cyclone's movement and projected trajectory.
These include the Multi Model Ensemble (MME) model and several global weather forecasting models.
Durai said that both RMC and IMD scientists had forecast an Andhra Pradesh landfall for Cyclone Akvan.

stories.title: Assam: Election Schedule Announced by Morigaon Xahitya Xabha for District Leadership
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: MORIGAON: The Morigaon District Xahitya Xabha has officially announced the upcoming elections for the posts of president, vice-president and secretary.
The election committee has already been formed.
The literary body announced Madharam Kakati as the chief election officer and Kumud Chandra Mahanta and Lakhikanta Sharma as election officers.
According to the schedule, the final voter list will be released on November 17 at 3 pm.
Nomination papers will be collected from November 18 to November 20 and filed from November 27 to November 29.
The nomination papers will be examined on November 30.
The counting of votes will be completed, and the results will be announced at the District Xahitya Xabha executive meeting on the same day.
The 29 branches of the Xahitya Xabha in the district will be eligible to participate in the elections.

stories.headline: Drugmulla school tragedy: MLA Baramulla says safety audit of buildings ignored despite repeated warnings
stories.title: Drugmulla school tragedy: MLA Baramulla says safety audit of buildings ignored despite repeated warnings
stories.summary: Srinagar, Nov 16: Member of Legislative Assembly (MLA) from Baramulla constituency, Javid Hassan Baigh Monday alleged that repeated warnings and recommendations for comprehensive safety audits of educational and healthcare institutions were ignored by the government, saying the tragic death of a class 3 student after a boundary wall collapsed at Government Middle School Drugmulla in Kupwara should serve as a wake-up call for the administration. In a post on social media, Baigh said the need for safety audits of public buildings and a dedicated disaster management mechanism was repeatedly highlighted by him over the years, but the concerns failed to receive the required attention. Recalling his tenure as Chairman of the Estimates Committee in 2015, Baigh said the committee recommended a comprehensive safety audit of all educational and healthcare buildings, followed by structures belonging to other government departments, commercial establishments and residential buildings. "I also strongly advocated the establishment of a dedicated Disaster Management Department with an effective presence in every district, equipped with infrastructure, logistics, trained manpower and resources," he said. MLA Baramulla said the department should conduct regular mock drills, public awareness programmes and training exercises, particularly given Jammu and Kashmir's vulnerability to earthquakes, floods and other natural disasters. Baigh said he had also moved a resolution in the Legislative Assembly on the issue, but it was "unfortunately not taken up for discussion." Baigh further claimed that he raised the matter during a meeting of education department in Jammu last year, "but my concerns were brushed aside." The MLA said he again urged senior government officers during the last meeting of the Estimates Committee, chaired by MLA Nazir Gurezi, to undertake comprehensive safety audits of existing buildings, beginning with educational and healthcare institutions. He however expressed disappointment that his suggestions regarding safety and disaster preparedness did not find mention in the committee's concluding remarks. Baigh said he also raised concerns over earthquake and flood vulnerabilities during a recent interaction with civil society members in Baramulla town and urged both the government and society not to overlook the potential threats. Reacting to the Dragmulla tragedy, the legislator said the death of the minor student was a failure of collective responsibility. "Schools are meant to provide safety, learning and protection rather than exposing children to life-threatening risks," he said. He called for establishing the exact circumstances that led to the student's death and fixing responsibility wherever negligence was established. "Accountability alone is not enough. There is a need for immediate corrective measures and proper safety audits of every school, hospital and public building," he added. He said the loss of a child's life could not be reversed, but systematic preventive measures could avert similar tragedies. MLA Baramulla urged the government to treat the incident as a warning against administrative indifference and ensure that human lives were not sacrificed "due to negligence or lack of preparedness."

stories.headline: Delhi Paharganj building collapse: FIR filed against property owner, contractor
stories.title: Delhi Paharganj building collapse: FIR filed against property owner, contractor
stories.summary: Eight people were injured after a portion of a building collapsed while the roof slab of its second floor was being laid during construction of a hotel in central Delhi’s Paharganj
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'building collapse' in title weight 46
article_sentences: An FIR was registered at the Paharganj police station on Monday (November 16, 2026) against the owner and contractor of the building that collapsed in Central Delhi’s Paharganj, injuring 8 people.

The FIR was registered under Sections 290 (negligent conduct with respect to buildings), 125(a) (act endangering life or personal safety), 223(a) (disobedience to an order duly promulgated by a public servant) and 3(5) (common intention) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), according to DCP (Central) Rohit Rajbir Singh.
“The property owner, Raman, and contractor Anwar have been apprehended and are being bound down.
Further investigation is underway,” he added.

Eight people were injured after a portion of a building collapsed while the roof slab of its second floor was being laid during construction of a hotel in central Delhi’s Paharganj on Sunday evening (November 15, 2026).
The incident took place at property numbers 3992–3993 in Kasheruwalan, Sangatrashan, opposite the Government Girls Senior Secondary School.
According to the police, construction work for a hotel was underway in the building when the roof slab (lanter) of the second floor was being laid.
A portion of the structure gave way, leaving eight people injured.
During an initial inspection, the supporting columns of the building were found to be wet and the structure appeared to have tilted, police said.

stories.headline: India’s wholesale inflation surges to 12.3% in October as energy prices rise
stories.title: India’s wholesale inflation surges to 12.3% in October as energy prices rise
stories.summary: Rising energy and commodity costs are increasing pressure on manufacturers, transport operators and businesses, economists said, while food inflation eased marginally
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: With a sharp rise in energy prices, wholesale inflation based on the Wholesale Price Index (WPI) surged to 12.3 per cent in October, data released by the Commerce & Industry Ministry on Monday showed.
The rate was 11.4 per cent in September.

“Year-on-Year inflation rates for major groups, namely, Primary Articles, Fuel and Power, and Manufactured Products are 9.24 per cent, 32.84 per cent, and 9.54 per cent, respectively in October 2026, compared to 8.67 per cent, 25.85 per cent, and 9.76 per cent, respectively in September 2026,” the Ministry said in a statement.

Across groups, ‘Mineral Oils (containing Petroleum Products)’, ‘Crude Petroleum and Natural Gas’, ‘Electricity’, ‘Food Articles’, ‘Manufacture of Basic Metals’, ‘Manufacture of Chemicals and Chemical Products’, ‘Manufacture of Food Products’, ‘Non-Food Articles’, ‘Manufacture of Textiles’, and ‘Manufacture of Rubber and Plastic Products’ have been drivers of WPI inflation in October.
The Food Index comprises ‘Food Articles’ from the Primary Articles major group and ‘Manufacture of Food Products’ from the Manufactured Products major group.
It observed an inflation of 8.58 per cent in October, compared to 8.66 per cent in September.

Pranjal Ghate, Economist at Brickwork Ratings, called the WPI as an energy story, with inflation in crude petroleum and natural gas reaching 70.80 per cent and Fuel and Power inflation surging to 32.84 per cent.
Meanwhile, manufactured products and food inflation moderated, suggesting limited broad-based price pressures.
However, he expects some relief ahead, with Brent crude declining by around $20 per barrel by mid-November.
If sustained, this should ease WPI pressures in the post-festive period and, with a lag, moderate CPI through lower input and transportation costs.

“We expect CPI inflation to peak at around 6 per cent in Q3 FY27 before moderating, though it is likely to remain above the RBI’s 4% target through the year,” he said while adding that the October WPI data reinforces the view that a further 25-basis-point repo rate hike to 5.75 per cent is highly likely, followed by a pause.

stories.title: Supreme Court asks Centre, States to file status reports on setting up of special courts to hear NDPS Act cases
stories.summary: Supreme Court took note of the submissions of Additional Solicitor General Aishwarya Bhati, appearing for the Centre, that not much progress has been made in pursuance of the orders passed by the apex court recently on setting up of special courts
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence

article_sentences: The Supreme Court on Monday (November 16, 2026) asked the Centre, State governments and Union Territory administrations to file fresh status reports on progress made in the establishment of 449 special courts to hear cases of heinous offences under the NDPS Act.

A Bench comprising Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana took note of the submissions of Additional Solicitor General Aishwarya Bhati, appearing for the Centre, that not much progress has been made in pursuance of the orders passed by the apex court recently on setting up of special courts.
"This is a three-judge matter also," Justice Bagchi said and referred to the non-availability of Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant for the hearing.

The Bench said that it will keep the suo motu case concerning the creation of exclusive special courts for speedy trials under the National Investigation Agency (NIA) Act and the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (NDPS) Act after a few weeks and preferably before the winter vacation in December.
It asked the Centre, States and Union Territories to file fresh status reports on the progress made by them in creating special courts for early disposal of pending cases under the NIA and NDPS Acts.
Earlier, the Bench had expressed concern over the alarming increase in narcotics-related offences across the country and the growing pendency of cases under the NDPS Act.
On September 7, the court had directed the Centre, State governments and Union Territory administrations to expedite the establishment of exclusive special courts, preferably within six weeks.
According to an affidavit filed by the Union government, 449 exclusive NDPS courts have been identified as necessary across the country to address the mounting backlog of cases.
The Centre had told the court that 176 of these courts were already operational.

Taking note of the figures, the Bench had observed that the existing pendency and the "unfortunate, alarming increase" in offences under the NDPS Act made it imperative to establish all the identified courts at the earliest.

The Bench had directed the Centre, State governments and Union Territory administrations to ensure the necessary infrastructure and appointment of adequate staff so that the remaining courts could become operational preferably within six weeks.
Apart from NDPS cases, the Bench also reviewed the progress made by States in establishing exclusive special courts for trials under Section 11 of the NIA Act, 2008.

stories.headline: Carney says Canada could turn to Chinese automakers if Trump trade talks fail
stories.title: Carney says Canada could turn to Chinese automakers if Trump trade talks fail
stories.summary: Phnom Penh, Nov 16: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney said that Canada could turn to Chinese automakers if trade negotiations with US President Donald Trump fail to preserve an integrated North American auto industry. Carney's comments in Cambodia on Monday came ahead of a planned meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping this week in Shenzhen, China, where Chinese auto manufacturing is expected to be discussed. The two leaders reached an agreement in January allowing tens of thousands of Chinese electric vehicles into Canada at reduced tariffs. “We have the best auto workers in the world, and we want them fully deployed, full opportunity, in an integrated North American market,” Carney told reporters in Cambodia. “That market has become less integrated because of US trade actions.” Carney said Saturday in Manila, Philippines, that any trade agreement with Washington must leave Canada with a viable auto industry. He said Monday that negotiations with the United States remain his priority, but their outcome could determine whether Canada pursues alternatives involving European, Chinese or Japanese automakers. Asked whether potential Chinese investment was leverage in the US negotiations, Carney replied: “It's not leverage. But action, reaction.” “If they're not fully utilised in a North American context, that provides other opportunities,” Carney said of Canada's auto workers and manufacturing assets. “Canada is going to move forward either way.” The Detroit Three — Ford, General Motors and Stellantis — operate factories across Canada, the United States and Mexico, with parts sometimes crossing borders multiple times before a vehicle is completed. Trump has repeatedly pushed automakers to move production to the United States from Canada. Carney said any Chinese investment would have to involve substantial manufacturing in Canada rather than simply assembling imported parts. He said it would require proper labour standards, manufacturing facilities and domestic supply chains that expand over time, including Canadian critical minerals used in electric vehicles. “It's not just about kit cars,” he said. “There has to be a manufacturing aspect involved.” Under the January agreement, Canada reduced its 100 per cent tariff on Chinese electric vehicles to 6.1 per cent, initially allowing up to 49,000 vehicles annually, with the cap increasing over time. In exchange, China agreed to lower tariffs on Canadian agricultural products, including canola. Carney said at the time that he expected the agreement to attract Chinese investment in Canada's auto industry and create jobs. The deal drew criticism from Ontario Premier Doug Ford, whose province is the centre of Canada's auto industry. Ford warned that allowing Chinese electric vehicles into Canada could threaten Canadian jobs and jeopardize access to the US market. Trump's tariffs have disrupted Canada's auto industry, which relies heavily on cross-border production. Canada recently threatened to sue Stellantis after the automaker shifted planned Jeep Compass production from Brampton, Ontario, to Illinois and agreed to sell its idled Canadian assembly plant. Carney said Saturday that he had spoken at length with Trump and senior US officials and that the two countries were making progress toward a possible trade agreement, although differences remained.

stories.headline: Statehood restoration, constitutional, democratic rights serve foundation for rebuilding trust: MP Chowdhary Mohammad Ramzan
stories.title: Statehood restoration, constitutional, democratic rights serve foundation for rebuilding trust: MP Chowdhary Mohammad Ramzan
stories.summary: Srinagar, Nov 15: The Jammu & Kashmir National Conference Additional General Secretary and MP Choudry Mohammad Ramzan said New Delhi will sooner or later have to reconsider the unconstitutional and undemocratic decisions of August 5, 2019, and restore Jammu and Kashmir’s special constitutional status. He said this while addressing an important party meeting held at the party headquarters, Nawa-e-Subh Complex. The meeting, as per a party statement, was attended by Provincial President Advocate Showkat Ahmad Mir, spokesperson Imran Nabi Dar, Provincial Secretary Syed Tawqeer Ahmad, Provincial President of the Women’s Wing Engineer Sabiya Qadri, Minority Cell Convener Jagdish Singh Azad, Provincial Youth President Mushtaq Mir and other party office-bearers. Chowdhary Mohammad Ramzan said that the unilateral abrogation of J&K’s special constitutional status on August 5, 2019, not only amounted to an injustice against the people of this historic region but also dealt a severe blow to the country’s federal democratic system and constitutional values. He said that Articles 370 and 35A were not merely constitutional provisions but also safeguards for the identity, distinct character, land rights, employment opportunities and constitutional rights of the people of Jammu and Kashmir. He stated that the history of the National Conference is marked by sacrifices and a sustained struggle for protecting the identity, autonomy and special constitutional status of Jammu and Kashmir. "From the leadership of Sher-e-Kashmir Sheikh Mohammad Abdullah to the present day, the party has consistently made sacrifices to safeguard the constitutional rights, dignity and political identity of the people. Despite political challenges, difficult circumstances and adverse conditions, the National Conference has never compromised on its principled position and will not do so in the future either," he added. He further said that the National Conference had raised its voice against the decisions of August 5, 2019, at every democratic, political, constitutional and legal forum. From Parliament to the Supreme Court, the party has continued its struggle for the restoration of the rights of the people of Jammu and Kashmir. He emphasised that the restoration of Articles 370 and 35A remains a fundamental part of the party’s political commitment and struggle. This struggle, he said, is not driven by any political interest or desire for power, but by the need to protect the constitutional rights, collective identity and future of generations to come.

stories.title: Ram temple donation theft: Congress seeks new SIT reporting exclusively to Supreme Court
stories.summary: Congress said that Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s “silence” on the issue is “deeply troubling” to the nation and asserted that those who have betrayed people’s faith must be held accountable
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: Escalating its attack on the BJP over the Ram temple donation theft case, the Congress on Monday (November 16, 2026) demanded that a new and independent SIT be constituted, reporting exclusively and directly to the Supreme Court, with a mandate to investigate all aspects of the matter.

The Opposition party also said that Prime Minister Narendra Modi's "silence" on the issue is "deeply troubling" to the nation and asserted that those who have betrayed people's faith must be held accountable.
In a post in Hindi on X, Congress general secretary in-charge communications.
Jairam Ramesh said, "Chanda Chori Aastha Dhokha.
As the saying goes, theft never remains hidden; sooner or later, it is bound to be exposed."

New revelations emerging daily regarding the theft of offerings at the Ram Mandir in Ayodhya are exposing the attempts by the Central and Uttar Pradesh governments to shield individuals associated with the BJP, RSS, and VHP, Mr. Ramesh claimed.
"The matter is no longer just about theft.
The question now arises: were both the public and the Supreme Court misled in the name of an investigation?
It is evident that two SITs (Special Investigation Teams) were constituted — one to pull the wool over the public's eyes, and the other over the Court," Mr. Ramesh said.

On July 20, the government informed the Supreme Court that the first team was not conducting an investigation and yet, on August 4, why did the Chief Minister, while speaking in the Legislative Assembly, cite the preliminary investigation conducted by that very same team, he asked.
On what basis was this done, and was the House provided with incorrect information, or was the Supreme Court misled, Mr. Ramesh questioned.
"If no investigation had taken place, then on the basis of which interim report did the Trust grant a 'clean chit' to Champat Rai on July 6?" he said.

stories.title: Future Wars: CDS Flags 5 Priorities For India's Defence Self-Reliance And Military Preparedness
stories.summary: At the ANI National Security Summit 3.0 in Delhi, Chief of Defence Staff General NS Raja Subramani outlined five key priorities for India's preparedness for future wars and achieving Aatmanirbharta in defence. He highlighted space capabilities, artificial intelligence and algorithmic warfare, indigenous defence manufacturing, modernisation of legacy military systems and talent development. Emphasising the growing importance of satellites for surveillance, communication and navigation, he called for stronger capabilities involving ISRO and private players. He also stressed the need for domestic industries to manufacture critical components at scale and develop advanced technologies, underlining that India's future military strength will depend on both technology and skilled talent.

stories.headline: India, US, eight other nations sign declaration to safeguard AI supply chains
stories.title: India, US, eight other nations sign declaration to safeguard AI supply chains
stories.summary: Washington, Nov 16: India, the US and eight other countries have signed a declaration to treat safeguarding artificial intelligence supply chains as a “shared endeavour” amid growing competition with China in emerging technology. The San Francisco Declaration was signed at a meeting of the founders of the US-led Pax Silica initiative convened by US Under Secretary of State for Economic Affairs Jacob Helberg on Sunday. The declaration was released by the Governments of the US, Australia, India, Israel, Japan, South Korea, Qatar, Singapore, the United Arab Emirates, and the United Kingdom. The Pax Silica initiative was announced by the US in December last year to secure supply chains for silicon and other minerals essential to semiconductor production and, by extension, to artificial intelligence and other advanced technological industries. The declaration on Sunday affirms that economic security is fundamental to national security, sets out the participants’ common understanding of the sensitive technologies and critical infrastructure that underpin Super Intelligence supply chains, and declares that safeguarding them is a shared endeavour, a State Department statement said. The US government refers to Artificial Intelligence (AI) as Super Intelligence (SI) after President Donald Trump signed an executive order to rename it. The Declaration on Secure Foundations of Enduring Prosperity also resolves to establish working groups to carry common purpose into common practice. It proposed to set up five groups covering pro-innovation policy frameworks, SI adoption in key sectors, supply chain cooperation across the SI stack, safe harbours and supply chain security hubs, and SI security and resilience. “No nation can secure the foundations of the SI era alone, and the prosperity SI makes possible will only be as durable as the supply chains and infrastructure beneath it,” the statement said. The declaration said that by agreeing on what must be protected and committing to protect it together, participants are laying the secure foundations on which partner nations can innovate, invest, and grow. “Less than a year after its launch, Pax Silica is entering a new phase. With the San Francisco Declaration, the coalition cements its shared principles into a working partnership with a common baseline and a path to act on it, the statement said.
